title: Tamsin and the Contact
premise: Marguerite 'Margo' Eriksen is the deniable man behind an embassy that exists on no map, cleaning up leaks and loose ends for handlers he's never met in person. When his own voiceprint unlocks a black server in Tallinn, he discovers 'the Contact' — a whistleblower inside the network who has scheduled a catastrophic infrastructure failure to be disguised as an industrial accident, timed to expose the embassy's crimes by killing thousands. Hunting the Contact across three countries, Margo realizes the voice is someone from his buried past, and that his own handlers intend to let the attack happen to bury their secrets with the dead. In the end Margo chooses truth over loyalty, exposing the embassy at the cost of his identity, and vanishes into the life of a man who officially never existed.
about_author: E. M. Quintana is the pen name of a former logistics consultant who spent a decade working contracts near diplomatic compounds before turning to fiction. Quintana writes thrillers about people whose jobs require them to be unmemorable, drawing on a fascination with paperwork as a weapon.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag
chapters.summary: POV: Marguerite Eriksen. Margo burns a compromised source's identity in Vienna, demonstrating his methodical craft and the polished lie of his daily life. A routine debrief call ends with an odd question from his handler: 'Do you still keep the bag packed?' The beat is quiet unease — the machinery he serves has begun watching him.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: POV: Margo. At 3 a.m., a server farm in Tallinn unlocks using Margo's authenticated voiceprint — a biometric he never surrendered willingly. Inside: schematics for a staged 'gas main accident' in Rotterdam and a countdown. His handler orders him to ignore it. The beat is dread; the tools of his trade are being used against him.

chapters.title: Deniable Man
chapters.summary: POV: Margo. Flying to Tallinn off-book, Margo reviews his own file smuggled from the server and finds gaps — years redacted even from him. He realizes the embassy has curated his memory of his own past. Emotional beat: vertigo, the first crack in his loyalty.

chapters.title: The Contact
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Margo / unknown whistleblower. The Contact messages Margo directly through the server: they know his real name, the one even he barely remembers. They claim the Rotterdam attack is the embassy's operation, not theirs. Beat: paranoia — hunter and hunted cannot tell who is which.

chapters.title: Old Streets
chapters.summary: POV: Margo. Following a lead to Riga, Margo walks streets from his erased childhood and meets a woman, Ilga, who recognizes his face without introduction. She gives him half a story about a boy taken by 'the office.' Beat: grief surfacing under tradecraft.

chapters.title: Housecleaning
chapters.summary: POV: secondary handler Voss. Voss activates a cleanup team with two targets: the Contact, and Margo if he goes dark. We see the institution's cold arithmetic — an acceptable casualty count in Rotterdam buys twenty years of silence. Beat: chilling institutional menace.

chapters.title: Dead Drop
chapters.summary: POV: Margo. A meet arranged by the Contact turns out to be bait — or a test. Margo survives an ambush only because the Contact calls off the shooters mid-attack, proving they have authority inside the network. Beat: whiplash trust; the enemy may be his only ally.

chapters.title: Ilga's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV: Margo. Ilga reveals she was the records clerk who processed children into the program, including Margo. Her ledger names the architect of the Rotterdam plan: Deputy Director Hale, Margo's ultimate superior. Beat: fury and betrayal compounding.

chapters.title: Rotterdam
chapters.summary: POV: Margo. On-site reconnaissance of the target facility confirms the accident scenario is engineered down to the weather reports. Margo must decide whether to stop it or let it burn the embassy down. Beat: moral fulcrum of the book.

chapters.title: The Voice
chapters.summary: POV: Margo. The Contact finally speaks live: it is Tomas, the boy who was taken alongside Margo — his childhood friend, presumed dead, now the network's security architect turned saboteur. Beat: recognition, relief, and immediate suspicion of what Tomas has become.

chapters.title: Two Truths
chapters.summary: POV: Tomas. Flashback chapter: Tomas's recruitment, his discovery of the Rotterdam plan, and why he used Margo's voiceprint — because Margo is the one man whose access can reach Hale's private authorization chain. Beat: sympathy for an extremist means to a just end.

chapters.title: Compromised
chapters.summary: POV: Margo. Voss's team finds Ilga; her ledger is seized but she escapes with one page. Margo learns his handler has reported him rogue. Every safehouse, account, and alias begins dying within hours. Beat: the deniable man made fully deniable.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: POV: Margo. Running on cash and forged papers, Margo negotiates with a rival intelligence service for sanctuary in exchange for the embassy's files — and realizes he'd be trading one master for another. Beat: temptation of the easy betrayal.

chapters.title: Hale
chapters.summary: POV: Hale. The antagonist's chapter: Hale genuinely believes the attack will save more lives than it costs by preventing war, and he considers Margo a son. Beat: power rationalizing itself; the reader almost agrees.

chapters.title: The Page
chapters.summary: POV: Margo. The rescued ledger page proves Hale personally authorized the 'accident' methodology years ago — this isn't containment, it's repetition. Margo commits fully to stopping the attack rather than exploiting it. Beat: decision crystallizes into resolve.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Margo/Tomas. With 60 hours left, Margo and Tomas plan to trigger the fail-safes manually, but Tomas refuses to abort entirely — he wants the world to see the attempt, casualties or not. Beat: allies fracture over means versus message.

chapters.title: Voss's Net
chapters.summary: POV: Voss. The cleanup team closes on both men in Antwerp; Voss, reading Hale's deeper game, quietly begins keeping her own insurance copies. Beat: the instrument developing doubts, seeding the finale's turn.

chapters.title: Antwerp Station
chapters.summary: POV: Margo. Ambush at the rail station; Margo saves Voss from a crossfire meant to erase her too, buying an uneasy truce and her silence. Beat: loyalty redefined person-to-person, institution abandoned.

chapters.title: The Facility
chapters.summary: POV: Margo/Tomas. Infiltration of the Rotterdam site hours before detonation; they disable the primary charge but Tomas triggers a partial release to guarantee headlines. Beat: climax of action and of the friends' moral split.

chapters.title: What the World Saw
chapters.summary: POV: multiple brief POVs. The partial event makes global news; investigators find Hale's fingerprints in the safety logs. Hale, cornered, offers Margo full restoration of his identity in exchange for silence. Beat: the final temptation, stated in the currency of selfhood.

chapters.title: Truth Over Loyalty
chapters.summary: POV: Margo. Margo refuses, delivers the complete archive to journalists and prosecutors via Voss's insurance copies, and watches Hale arrested as the embassy is formally disavowed. Tomas surrenders to face trial, asking Margo to remember the boy he was. Beat: catharsis at cost.

chapters.title: A Man Who Never Existed
chapters.summary: POV: Margo. Months later, 'Marguerite Eriksen' is a closed file. Living under a new name near Ilga, Margo unpacks — for the first time — instead of packing. He keeps one item from the go-bag: the ledger page. Beat: quiet resolution; identity rebuilt from truth, not assignment.
